record.paper_title: Open problems in Gaussian fluid queueing theory
record.original_question: Consider a fluid queue with constant output rate c > 0 whose stationary buffer content process is Q(t), where the input is a centered Gaussian process X(t) with stationary increments, continuous sample paths, and variance function σ_X^2(t). Is the short-range or long-range dependence behavior of the input process X(·) inherited by the workload process Q(t), equivalently by the large-time behavior of the correlation function ρ(t)=Corr(Q(t),Q(0))?

evidence.quote: Let {Q(t) : t ≥ 0} be the stationary buffer content process for a fluid queue fed by a centered Gaussian stochastic process {X(t) : t ∈ R} with stationary increments, continuous sample paths a.s. and variance function σ2_X(t) = Var(X(t)). We assume that the system is emptied with a constant output rate c > 0.

From a more general standpoint, an interesting and important fundamental question can be stated: is the short/long-range dependence property on the level of input process X(·) inherited by the workload process?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{X(t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}$ be a centered Gaussian stochastic process with stationary increments, almost surely continuous sample paths, and variance function $\sigma_X^2(t)=\mathrm{Var}(X(t))$. Fix a constant output rate $c>0$ such that the associated fluid queue is stable, and let $\{Q(t):t\geq 0\}$ denote the stationary buffer content (workload) process defined by
$$Q(t)=\sup_{s\leq t}\bigl(X(t)-X(s)-c(t-s)\bigr).$$
Define the workload correlation function $\rho(t)=\mathrm{Corr}(Q(t),Q(0))$ for $t\geq 0$.

Recall that $X$ is said to exhibit short-range dependence if its increment correlations are summable (or decay sufficiently fast, e.g. exponentially), and long-range dependence if they decay only polynomially and are non-summable.

Question: Is the short-range or long-range dependence property of the input process $X(\cdot)$ inherited by the workload process $Q(\cdot)$? Equivalently, does the large-$t$ decay rate of $\rho(t)$ match that of the covariance structure of $X$ — for instance, exponential decay of $\rho(t)$ when $X$ is short-range dependent, and polynomial decay of $\rho(t)$ at the same rate as the covariance of the increments of $X$ when $X$ is long-range dependent?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the short/long-range dependence of a Gaussian input is inherited by the workload correlation function in a Gaussian fluid queue is identified as an open problem; only the Brownian queue case (exponential decay) is known, while the polynomial decay conjecture for long-range dependent inputs remains unresolved in general. Simulation-based studies and related work on Lévy-driven queues and tandem fluid queues address adjacent cases but do not settle the general Gaussian inheritance question.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in Gaussian fluid queueing theory
status_evidence.snippet: Three challenging open problems originate from the asymptotic analysis of Gaussian fluid queueing models, including the correlation structure of the stationary buffer content process.
status_evidence.claim: The correlation inheritance question is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Simulation-Based Computation of the Workload Correlation Function in a Lévy-Driven Queue
status_evidence.snippet: Simulation-based methods are used to estimate the workload correlation function, since closed-form expressions are unavailable beyond the Brownian case.
status_evidence.claim: Outside of the Brownian queue, the workload correlation function is not known in closed form, supporting the open status.

status_evidence.title: Tandem fluid queue with long-range dependent inputs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work investigates fluid queues with long-range dependent (fractional Brownian) input, indicating ongoing research on dependence inheritance.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is the subject of ongoing recent research rather than being settled.
